title: 30 Google Secrets You’ll Wish You Knew Years Ago
partialText: Think you know Google? Think again—hidden deep within that simple search bar is a subterranean network of secret search operators, hidden diagnostic tools, and buried privacy toggles that change everything. From listening to your saved voice logs to uncovering secret files and bypassing algorithm bubbles, here are 30 game-changing Google secrets you were never supposed to find.

title: 15 Reddit Scandals That Changed the Internet Forever
partialText: Reddit’s biggest controversies are platform-design lessons in disguise. From GameStop and API protests to misinformation, moderator revolts, and online witch hunts, each one shows what happens when community systems fail under pressure.

title: 5 Creative Type Foundries You Should Know About
partialText: Forget the same safe fonts you see on every other website. These five independent foundries are making typography weird, expressive and impossible to ignore—and they might convince you to never reach for Inter again.

title: She Taught the Macintosh to Smile
partialText: The Macintosh didn’t always smile. Susan Kare gave it one — and with a handful of black pixels, helped transform the computer from an intimidating machine into something that felt human. More than 40 years later, we’re still speaking the visual language she helped create.

title: The Death of the Portfolio (And What to Do Before You’re Left Behind)
partialText: A polished portfolio used to get you hired. Now AI makes polished work cheap, and clients want proof you can solve problems, communicate clearly, and deliver today.

title: Web Design Schools Have a Giant YouTube University Problem — And AI Just Made It Worse
partialText: A web design degree used to be the obvious way to learn the craft. Now it’s competing with YouTube, AI, and people who spend those same years actually building things — so if universities can’t offer something better, students have every right to ask what they’re paying for.

title: Web Designers Love Dark Mode Toggles. Users Might Not Care.
partialText: Dark mode toggles are everywhere, but do users actually need them, or are designers designing for other designers? A growing UX debate is questioning whether that little sun-and-moon button deserves permanent space in your website’s header.

title: Turn Any Photo Into Retro ASCII Art in Seconds
partialText: Turn any photo into gloriously retro ASCII art — made entirely from letters, symbols, and tiny bits of chaos. This free tool turns your dog, face, logo, or worst holiday photo into something that belongs on a 1980s terminal. You will absolutely waste 10 minutes on it.

title: How the Prompt Box is Swallowing Website Interfaces Whole
partialText: For decades, web designers obsessed over perfecting menus, tabs, and dropdowns. Now a single empty prompt box is quietly replacing them all. As AI turns websites into conversations, we're gaining incredible speed—but we may be losing something unexpected: the joy of discovery.

title: Traditional Web Development is Dead…(and Honestly? Good Riddance.)
partialText: AI isn't killing web development—it’s killing the boring parts. The real winners won't be the people who can memorize another framework. They'll be the builders who can spot opportunities, solve business problems, and launch products that once required entire teams. The age of the one-person software company has arrived.

title: This Website Found More Than 5 Million Forgotten iPhone Videos… and It’s Weirdly Emotional
partialText: Before TikTok turned every moment into content, people uploaded shaky, pointless little iPhone videos to YouTube and forgot about them. This strange website found five million of them—dogs, holidays, car rides, bad concerts—and lets you fall into a random stranger’s 2010 afternoon.

title: Canva Just Turned Affinity Into Adobe’s Biggest Free Problem
partialText: Canva just made a much more serious play for professional designers: Affinity now brings design, photo editing, and layout into one free app, while Canva connects it to motion, AI, and team-friendly publishing tools.

title: Nobody Wants Your Damn App
partialText: Nobody wants another app cluttering their phone—so why does every website keep begging us to install one? The web already perfected the experience: click, load, done.  Maybe it’s time we stopped trying to ruin it.

title: This Weird 1973 Typeface Just Came Back From the Dead
partialText: A wonderfully weird typeface from 1973 has come back to life — and somehow it looks more at home in 2026 than ever. Meet Clippy, the retro font that bends, rocks and wobbles its way into the digital age.

title: The Death of Apps Has Already Begun
partialText: We spent 15 years filling our phones with apps. AI could make almost all of them invisible... and the death of apps may already be closer than anyone realizes.

title: AI Can Build Your UI. Now Figma Can Tell It When It Screwed Up.
partialText: AI can now build a UI in seconds, but that doesn't mean it built the UI you actually designed. A new Applitools integration turns Figma designs into visual baselines, automatically catching the subtle differences AI coding agents leave behind before they make it into production.

title: 25 Places Designers Can Still Find Free, Non-AI Images for Commercial Use
partialText: AI images are taking over stock libraries, but the human-made web isn't dead yet. We found 25 places where designers can still find incredible free, real photography, art, and imagery for commercial use.

title: Chrome Can Now Measure Exactly How Obnoxious Your Website’s Ads Are
partialText: Chrome can now measure exactly how obnoxious a website’s ads are, from how much of your screen they swallow to how much data and CPU time they burn. Those ad-stuffed websites can finally be measured, and the results are public.
